hops.afterHeading: A growth cone that folds up
hops.title: Why cut spinal axons stall at the injury
hops.text: Adult central axons usually regrow poorly after injury. In 1981 Samuel David and Albert Aguayo showed the cells themselves are not the only limit: axons from injured adult rat medulla and spinal cord grew about thirty millimetres when handed a peripheral-nerve bridge. After spinal cord injury in adult rats, some scar-forming cells increase Sema3A gene expression, and Sema3A collapses sensitive growth cones in culture. In 2003 chemists in Osaka fished a Sema3A blocker named xanthofulvin out of a Penicillium mold broth, and a Keio University group later ran it into transected adult rat cords for four weeks: more axons regenerated or survived, and the rats moved better.

sources.citation: David S & Aguayo AJ, Science 214:931-933 (1981), PMID 6171034.
Kikuchi K et al., J Biol Chem 278:42985-42991 (2003), PMID 12933805.
Kaneko S et al., Nat Med 12:1380-1389 (2006), PMID 17099709.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A glass petri dish holding a fuzzy blue-green mold colony with tiny golden droplets on a wooden lab bench.
image.caption: A compound from a Penicillium mold blocks Sema3A, and cut rat spinal axons fared better with it.

hops.title: A poxvirus with a semaphorin gene
hops.text: Vaccinia, a poxvirus, carries a semaphorin of its own, called A39R. In 1998 researchers used the viral protein as bait to pull its receptor out of a human B cell line and landed on a new plexin, later named Plexin-C1, which turns up on immune cells such as dendritic cells. In 2005 Thierry Walzer and colleagues put A39R on cultured mouse dendritic cells. The cells stayed alive, but they rearranged their actin, loosened their integrin grip, drew their edges in, and fewer of them moved toward a chemokine signal. That actin rearrangement, weaker adhesion and retraction match a growth cone's collapse response, performed by an immune cell.

sources.citation: Comeau MR et al., Immunity 8:473-482 (1998), PMID 9586637.
Walzer T et al., J Immunol 174:51-59 (2005), PMID 15611227.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A pale-blue dendritic cell rounding up as its projections retract in culture medium on a clear glass surface.
image.caption: A viral semaphorin made cultured dendritic cells pull in their edges and migrate less.

hops.title: Sema3A in your skin
hops.text: Cells in your epidermis make Sema3A, which helps limit the sensory nerve sprouting that NGF encourages. Several studies of atopic dermatitis, the common form of eczema, report lower epidermal Sema3A protein and more epidermal nerve fibres, whereas another found the highest SEMA3A gene expression in atopic dermatitis among three itch disorders and lower epidermal fibre density across all three, leaving the human picture unsettled. The mouse experiment is cleaner: in NC/Nga mice with eczema-like skin, a recombinant Sema3A ointment reduced epidermal nerve fibre density, eased skin inflammation and cut scratching compared with controls.

sources.citation: Tominaga M & Takamori K, J Dermatol 41:205-212 (2014), PMID 24628070.
Negi O et al., J Dermatol Sci 66:37-43 (2012), PMID 22381253.
Agelopoulos K et al., J Invest Dermatol 143:264-272.e3 (2023), PMID 36075451.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A small unlabelled glass jar of pale ointment with its lid beside it on a clean laboratory bench.
image.caption: A Sema3A ointment reduced epidermal nerve fibre density and scratching in mice with eczema-like skin.

audio.title: Semaphorins and their receptors in the nose, teeth and bone
audio.transcript:
Semaphorins are named for semaphore signal flags, and they were found as axon guidance cues. Follow the family and its receptors out of the embryo's nervous system, though, and you end up in three places you would not expect: a human nose, a newborn tooth, and the inside of a bone.

Start with the catcher rather than the cue. Furin, a human enzyme, can trim the tail of some class three semaphorins, exposing an arginine that fits one binding pocket on neuropilin one. In two thousand twenty, two papers published back to back in the same issue of Science found another protein that fits that pocket. When furin cuts the spike protein of SARS coronavirus two, one fragment of the spike gains a newly exposed end, arginine, arginine, alanine, arginine, that binds neuropilin one directly. Blocking neuropilin one, with interfering R N A, with inhibitors, or with a blocking antibody, reduced viral entry and infectivity in cultured cells. And in autopsy tissue from people who died of COVID nineteen, the virus was found infecting neuropilin one positive cells in the olfactory epithelium, right at the surface facing the nasal cavity. In nineteen ninety-seven, developmental neurobiologists identified neuropilin as a semaphorin receptor. Twenty-three years later, virologists were studying the same protein.

Now move to the mouth. A spoonful of ice cream can send a jolt through a sensitive tooth, and sensory nerves in the soft pulp carry that pain signal. Early in a tooth's development, though, those fibres stay outside the pulp. In newborn mice, sensory fibres do not enter the pulp of the first lower molar until enamel formation has started, about day three after birth, and they only begin weaving their network at the pulp and dentin border around day seven. In two thousand twelve, researchers at the University of Bergen looked at newborn mice that lacked Sema three A. Without that repulsive rope line, thin, unbundled fibres were already in the pulp of the first lower molar on the day of birth, three days early, and by day two they had formed an enlarged network, whereas controls only begin forming one on day seven.

Finally, step into bone, where Sema three A also changes how bone cells develop. Remember the lesson's rule: the cue marks the place, and the receiving cell decides what it means. Your skeleton is maintained by two crews. Osteoclasts dissolve old bone, osteoblasts build new bone. In two thousand twelve, a group in Tokyo showed that Sema three A acts through neuropilin one in cultures of osteoclast precursors and osteoblast precursors. On osteoclast precursors it held back the formation of the demolition crew. In calvarial cell cultures, it favoured the development of bone-building cells, and in separate bone marrow stromal cell cultures, it held back the development of fat cells. Both effects favour bone gain in those experiments, and in the animal, mice lacking Sema three A, or carrying a neuropilin one that cannot bind it, had low bone mass. Later work challenged how much of that happens directly on bone cells in a living animal: mice lacking Sema three A only in bone-building cells kept normal bone mass, while mice lacking it in neurons had fewer sensory fibres in bone and built less bone, so how much of the signal acts locally and how much acts through nerves is still argued over. In two mouse experiments, Sema three A delivered into the bloodstream increased spongy bone near the end of the femur, and local treatment increased regenerated cortical bone at a drill-hole injury. One cue, two kinds of bone cell, and a role in shaping bone that still involves sensory nerves.
